residencyRequirements.description: The petition is filed where the marriage was solemnized, or where the parties last resided together, or where the respondent resides, or where the petitioner resides (at the time of filing when the wife is the petitioner). See HMA s.19 / SMA s.31 / IDA s.3.

waitingPeriod.description: Mutual consent: 6-month cooling-off period between First Motion and Second Motion (HMA s.13B(2) / SMA s.28(2)). The Supreme Court in Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur (2017) 8 SCC 746 held courts may waive the 6-month cooling-off period. The Delhi High Court Full Bench (December 2025, MAT.APP.(FC) 111/2025) further held that the 1-year separation requirement under s.13B(1) is directory, not mandatory, and can be waived under s.14(1) proviso in cases of exceptional hardship or exceptional depravity. Both the 1-year and 6-month periods are waivable independently, and if waived, the decree may be made effective forthwith. Contested: no fixed waiting period.

noFault.name: Mutual Consent
noFault.description: Both spouses jointly petition for divorce after living separately for at least one year. A 6-month cooling-off period applies (waivable per Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur (2017)). The Delhi HC Full Bench (Dec 2025) held the 1-year separation requirement is also waivable under s.14(1) in cases of exceptional hardship/depravity.

fault.name: Adultery
fault.description: Spouse has had voluntary sexual intercourse with any person other than the petitioner after solemnization of the marriage.

fault.name: Cruelty
fault.description: Spouse has treated the petitioner with cruelty (physical or mental).

fault.name: Desertion
fault.description: Spouse has deserted the petitioner for a continuous period of not less than two years.

fault.name: Conversion
fault.description: Spouse has ceased to be a Hindu/has converted to another religion (HMA only).

fault.name: Unsoundness of Mind
fault.description: Spouse has been incurably of unsound mind or suffering continuously from mental disorder.

fault.name: Venereal Disease
fault.description: Spouse has been suffering from a venereal disease in communicable form.

fault.name: Renunciation of the World
fault.description: Spouse has renounced the world by entering any religious order (HMA only).

fault.name: Presumed Dead
fault.description: Spouse has not been heard of as being alive for a period of seven years or more.

wifeAdditional.name: Bigamy (wife only)
wifeAdditional.description: The husband had another wife living at the time of the marriage (applies only to marriages solemnized before the Hindu Marriage Act commenced on 18 May 1955).

wifeAdditional.name: Rape, Sodomy, or Bestiality by Husband (wife only)
wifeAdditional.description: The husband has been guilty of rape, sodomy, or bestiality since the solemnization of the marriage.

terminology.maritalProperty: No specific matrimonial property regime; Hindu Succession Act 1956 / court-ordered settlement

basic.name: Petition for Divorce

basic.description: Sworn affidavit on judicial stamp paper supporting the petition

basic.description: Original or certified copy of marriage certificate

Maintenance for wife, children, and parents

filingFees.notes: Filing fee varies by court. Indigent persons may apply for fee waiver. Court fees for mutual consent divorce are typically lower.

childSupportGuidelines.guidelines: No statutory formula; court considers income, needs, and lifestyle of the child
childSupportGuidelines.notes: BNSS s.144 (CrPC s.125) provides for maintenance; amount at court's discretion based on income and means of the respondent

spousalSupportGuidelines.guidelines: HMA s.25 (permanent alimony) / s.24 (maintenance pendente lite); SMA s.36-37; BNSS s.144
spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: No fixed formula. Court considers duration of marriage, earning capacity, standard of living, and conduct of parties.

effectiveDateRule: The decree takes effect from the date it is passed. For mutual consent, the decree is granted at the Second Motion hearing (after the 6-month cooling-off period, unless waived).
certificateNote: A certified copy of the decree may be obtained from the court registry after the decree is passed.
